subject: ent
title: Granulomatous Sinonasal Disease and Maxillectomy

steps.tx: **Mikulicz cells** are the histological signature of rhinoscleroma: large vacuolated macrophages stuffed with Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis bacilli, accompanied by plasma cells and Russell bodies in nasal biopsy tissue. Their presence separates rhinoscleroma from tuberculosis, leprosy and fungal granulomas that share the clinical stage. Examiners pair this cell with the woody Hebra nose and staged progression toward sclerotic stenosis.
steps.say: Large vacuolated macrophages stuffed with bacilli confirm rhinoscleroma under the microscope definitively. Plasma cells with Russell bodies are present in biopsy tissue alongside the characteristic cells. Woody hardening of the external nose completes the clinical picture externally.

vis.alt: Sagittal head cross section and histology showing rhinoscleroma nasal mass with Mikulicz cells on microscopy.
vis.caption: Rhinoscleroma with Mikulicz cells on histology. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Granulomatosis with polyangiitis** is a systemic small vessel vasculitis whose sinonasal disease crusts, bleeds and perforates the septum, sometimes collapsing the nasal bridge into a saddle deformity. Lung nodules and glomerulonephritis complete the classic triad, and cytoplasmic antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies against proteinase three support diagnosis. Limited sinonasal disease can precede systemic spread by years, so serology and urinary review accompany every destructive nasal granuloma.
steps.say: Small vessel vasculitis crusts and perforates the nose while threatening lungs and kidneys systemically. Specific antibody testing supports diagnosis alongside biopsy and urinary screening for renal disease. Nasal disease alone can precede systemic spread by years of limited involvement.

vis.alt: Diagram of granulomatosis with polyangiitis classic triad affecting upper airway with saddle nose, lungs and kidneys, often with c-ANCA positivity.
vis.caption: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis: airway, lung and kidney triad. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The **lethal midline granuloma** label historically described relentlessly destructive midface ulceration, most now reclassified as extranodal NK or T cell lymphoma, nasal type, strongly linked to Epstein Barr virus. Angiocentric growth destroys vessels and tissue, producing palatal perforation and midface collapse that mimics vasculitis clinically. Biopsies need generous tissue with immunophenotyping and viral studies because surface samples repeatedly return only necrosis.
steps.say: Relentless midface destruction once called lethal granuloma usually proves to be nasal lymphoma nowadays. Vessel centred growth destroys tissue and perforates the palate progressively over months. Deep generous biopsies with immune and viral studies succeed where surface samples show necrosis.

steps.tx: **NK/T cell lymphoma** of nasal type presents with nasal blockage, blood stained discharge and progressive midline destruction in middle aged adults, with systemic fever and weight loss as disease advances. Epstein Barr virus encoded RNA stains positively in tumour cells and plasma viral load tracks disease activity. Radiotherapy anchors treatment for localised disease, with asparaginase based chemotherapy added for advanced stages because conventional anthracyclines perform poorly.
steps.say: Nasal lymphoma of natural killer lineage destroys midline structures progressively with systemic symptoms advancing. Viral staining confirms lineage while blood viral load tracks activity during therapy monitoring. Radiation anchors localised treatment, with asparaginase regimens added for advanced disease.

steps.tx: Tuberculosis and fungal infection remain treatable mimics in the granuloma differential, so every destructive nasal biopsy is split for histology, culture and molecular tests before immunosuppression begins. Starting steroids or rituximab over undiagnosed infection converts local disease into dissemination. **Septal perforation** alone has a wider differential still, including cocaine use, trauma, surgery and cautery, which history must exclude before labelling vasculitis.
steps.say: Infection mimics vasculitis closely enough that biopsy material must reach culture and molecular laboratories routinely. Immunosuppression over undiagnosed infection risks dangerous dissemination of tuberculosis or fungus systemically. Cocaine, trauma and prior surgery explain many septal perforations without systemic disease.

steps.tx: **Maxillectomy** removes part or all of the maxilla for cancer clearance, graded from limited medial resection through infrastructure and subtotal operations to total maxillectomy with or without orbital exenteration. The defect separates mouth from nose and orbit, so reconstruction with an obturator prosthesis or free flap restores speech, swallowing and facial support. Preoperative dental impressions preserve obturator fit when prosthetic rehabilitation is the chosen route.
steps.say: Removing part or all of the upper jaw clears cancer with margins around the tumour. Resulting defects joining mouth to nose need prosthesis or flap reconstruction for speech and swallowing. Dental impressions before surgery preserve fit when an obturator is planned.

steps.tx: Orbital preservation in maxillary cancer surgery is decided by invasion, not proximity: tumour breaching periorbita or involving orbital fat, muscles or apex mandates exenteration, while displaced but intact orbital walls permit preservation with reconstruction. Preoperative imaging plus frozen section assessment guide this life changing choice. **Eye preservation** with a non seeing painful eye serves nobody, so function rather than anatomy alone settles borderline decisions.
steps.say: Invasion rather than mere proximity decides whether the eye survives maxillary cancer surgery. Breached periosteum or involved fat and muscle mandates removal for clearance margins. Function settles borderline choices because preserving a blind painful eye helps nobody.

left.title: Preserve the orbit
points: No fat, muscle or apex invasion

steps.tx: Adjuvant radiotherapy follows maxillectomy for close margins, perineural invasion, nodal disease or advanced stage, with concurrent chemotherapy added for the highest risk features in fit patients. Dental extraction of in field teeth, fluoride prophylaxis and trismus exercises precede radiation to reduce osteoradionecrosis. **Prosthetic review** continues lifelong because defects remodel, obturators loosen and recurrence hides beneath prostheses that are not removed at examination.
steps.say: Radiation follows surgery for close margins, nerve invasion or nodal disease in most advanced cases. Dental clearance and jaw exercises before radiation reduce bone death and stiffness afterwards. Prostheses must lift at every review because recurrence hides underneath them.

vis.title: Post maxillectomy adjuvant care
rows: Close margins, nerve or nodal risk

steps.tx: Surveillance after sinonasal cancer combines endoscopy, periodic magnetic resonance imaging and neck review, intensified over the first three years when most recurrences appear. New epistaxis, pain, loose prosthesis fit or cranial nerve symptoms between visits trigger urgent reassessment. **Late recurrence** still occurs in olfactory neuroblastoma after ten years, stretching its surveillance well beyond the standard five year horizon applied to squamous cancers.
steps.say: Endoscopy and periodic resonance imaging dominate surveillance during the first three high risk years. New bleeding, pain or loose prosthesis fit triggers urgent reassessment between scheduled visits. Vault tumours recur even after ten years, stretching their follow up horizon.

steps.tx: The granuloma cluster resolves into testable signatures. Mikulicz cells mean rhinoscleroma, cytoplasmic antibodies with lung and kidney disease mean vasculitis, viral positive angiocentric lymphoma explains lethal midline destruction, and sporangia mean rhinosporidiosis. Maxillectomy extent follows tumour extent, orbit follows invasion, and adjuvant therapy follows margin and nerve risk. **Biopsy adequacy** decides everything upstream, so deep tissue beats repeated surface sampling.
steps.say: Characteristic cells, antibodies, viral lymphoma and sporangia separate four destructive nasal diseases reliably. Resection extent follows tumour extent while orbital sacrifice follows proven invasion only. Deep adequate biopsy decides everything upstream, beating repeated necrotic surface samples.

cards.b: Large vacuolated macrophages containing Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis in rhinoscleroma, with plasma cells and Russell bodies.
Usually extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma, nasal type, EBV positive and angiocentric; radiotherapy plus asparaginase therapy.
Preserve when periorbita intact; exenterate when fat, muscle or apex invaded or eye blind and painful.

keys: Split granuloma biopsies for histology, culture and molecular tests
Never immunosuppress a destructive nasal lesion before excluding infection
Maxillectomy defects need obturator or flap rehabilitation
